thesis: Frontier AI is a small number of sparse Transformers whose capability now comes as much from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards and from reasoning at inference time as from pretraining scale. Open weights sit at or near the frontier, months behind rather than generations. Models complete substantial multi-step work where outcomes can be checked, and are supervised because they fail in ways they cannot detect. They remain frozen after release, with memory built around the weights rather than inside them.

dimensions.name: Compute
dimensions.baseline: Frontier training remains concentrated in a few large compute holders, while frontier-level capability is reproducible far more cheaply than a year earlier.
dimensions.incentive: Reduce the compute and cost required for frontier capability.
dimensions.inflection: Frontier-level capability becomes reproducible without frontier-scale infrastructure at all.
evidence: DeepSeek-R1 released with reported training costs orders of magnitude below Western frontier runs — 2025-01
Distillation of large reasoning models into small open models becomes routine — 2025
Inference costs continue falling sharply across providers — 2025
Frontier labs announce datacentre commitments at the tens-of-billions scale — 2025
Serving cost, not training cost, increasingly described as the binding constraint for reasoning models — 2025

dimensions.name: Architecture
dimensions.baseline: Transformers remain the frontier architecture; sparsity and long context are assumed rather than notable.
dimensions.incentive: Improve capability or efficiency beyond what the dominant architecture permits.
dimensions.inflection: A different architecture or capability mechanism meaningfully challenges Transformer dominance at the frontier.
evidence: Every frontier release of the year is a Transformer, near-universally mixture-of-experts — 2025
Hybrid attention/state-space models ship at production scale without displacing attention — 2025
Architectural effort concentrates on serving efficiency rather than on replacing the Transformer — 2025
Long context is a product feature rather than a research frontier — 2025

dimensions.name: Scaling
dimensions.baseline: Capability comes from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards and inference-time reasoning as much as from pretraining scale.
dimensions.incentive: Find additional ways to increase capability beyond pretraining scale.
dimensions.inflection: A scaling axis beyond pretraining and reinforced reasoning materially changes how capability is produced.
evidence: DeepSeek-R1 demonstrates reasoning emerging from RL on verifiable rewards, with the recipe published — 2025-01
Reasoning models become the default frontier product line across labs — 2025
Reported returns to pretraining scale alone widely described as diminishing — 2025
Verifiable-reward RL concentrated in mathematics and code, where answers can be checked — 2025
Synthetic and model-generated training data in routine frontier use — 2025

dimensions.name: Access
dimensions.baseline: Open-weight models are at or near the closed frontier, and the gap is measured in months.
dimensions.incentive: Make frontier capability cheaper, open or broadly accessible.
dimensions.inflection: Open-weight models lead rather than follow the closed frontier.
evidence: DeepSeek-R1 released with open weights and a published RL recipe, matching closed reasoning models on public benchmarks — 2025-01
Chinese open-weight labs sustain a rapid release cadence through the year — 2025
Open reasoning models become widely self-hosted in production — 2025
The strongest publicly reported systems remain closed at year end — 2025
Open-weight releases increasingly ship under genuinely permissive licences — 2025

dimensions.name: Agency
dimensions.baseline: Models complete substantial multi-step work in verifiable domains, and are supervised because they fail in ways they cannot detect.
dimensions.incentive: Make models able to reliably complete useful work with less human intervention.
dimensions.inflection: Models complete extended real work reliably enough to be left unsupervised.
evidence: Agentic coding tools reach broad professional use, running for many steps against real repositories — 2025
Reported SWE-bench Verified resolution rates rise substantially over 2024 — 2025
Computer-use and browser agents ship as products — 2025
Long-horizon reliability remains the limiting factor; human review remains standard practice — 2025
Agent capability is markedly stronger where outcomes are checkable than where they are not — 2025

dimensions.name: Persistence
dimensions.baseline: Models are static after training; memory is a product feature built around the weights, not learning inside them.
dimensions.incentive: Let a deployed model accumulate and retain what it encounters, cheaply.
dimensions.inflection: A deployed model's capability improves from its own use without a new training run.
evidence: Assistant memory features ship widely, storing retrieved text rather than updating weights — 2025
Weights remain frozen at release across every frontier product — 2025
Context windows and retrieval continue to substitute for retention — 2025
Continual-learning results remain research-stage and are not deployed at the frontier — 2025
